summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 20% to Rs 1,138 crore and EBITDA 34% to Rs 101 crore, while branded formulation grew only 3%.
summary.overview: Dharmaj Crop Guard reported FY26 revenue of Rs 1,138 crore (+20% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 101 crore (+34%) and net profit of Rs 55 crore (+57%). Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 234 crore (+11% YoY) against a stronger base. Growth was driven by domestic institutional formulation (+15%), exports recovery and a 37% rise in domestic active ingredient sales, while branded formulation was muted at 3% due to uneven monsoon and channel destocking. The technical plant reached PBT break-even in FY26, and management guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20%.

segments.name: Branded formulation (B2C)
segments.commentary: FY26 growth of 3%, with Q1 the strongest quarter and Q2 and Rabi weak due to erratic monsoon and channel inventory. Management guides 20-25% growth if monsoon is normal; new states contributed 14% of sales vs 7% last year.

segments.name: Domestic institutional formulation
segments.commentary: FY26 growth of 15%, described as consistent across the year.

segments.name: Domestic active ingredient (technical)
segments.commentary: Domestic sales up 37% in FY26; capacity utilisation 65-70%; EBITDA about 5% (vs negative in FY25); GP margin 22% vs 19%; PBT break-even reached.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Strong comeback in FY26 after weak FY25; GP margin 15-20%, EBITDA margin 10-12%; registrations in 2-3 new countries; Iran and Iraq shipments disrupted.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall top-line growth guided at 18-20%, with each vertical targeted at similar growth.
Company EBITDA margin (9% currently) to improve by 0.5-0.75 percentage points in FY27.
Technical plant EBITDA to reach 8-10% at optimal utilisation, but over 2-3 years; utilisation expected near 75% in FY27.
Herbicide facility in Kerala GIDC, Ahmedabad expected to be commissioned in Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex about Rs 50 crore; employee cost growth 5-8%, fixed costs broadly flat.
Management expects the branded formulation seasonal headwind to normalise in FY27.
capex_capacity: Technical plant utilisation 65-70% in FY26 (58% in the first year of operation), targeted near 75% in FY27.
New dedicated herbicide facility at Kerala GIDC, Ahmedabad: machinery being ordered, installation 4-5 months, commissioning Q3 FY27.
Existing herbicide unit to be converted to insecticide and fungicide production, freeing space at the formulation site.
FY27 capex about Rs 50 crore; management said it would be spent in the current year and would support growth for about three years.
demand_pricing: Branded formulation hit by erratic late-Q2 monsoon in August-September and weak Rabi pest pressure; channel inventory was liquidated.
Technical realisations were under pressure through most of FY26 and recovered only after February 2026, driven by input cost increases linked to the West Asia crisis.
Company says price increases pass on raw-material cost inflation with a 1-2% non-recoverable portion; prices revised frequently.
Management said paraquat ban in Andhra Pradesh would have no material volume impact (not even 1%).
Early-season (April-May) sales were on plan, with June sales dependent on the monsoon onset.

qa_highlights.question: What is the branded formulation B2B/B2C split outlook and marketing spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2C marketing is about 3% of B2C business; B2B share has risen; tolling outside the company will be brought in-house as herbicide capacity comes on line.

qa_highlights.question: Technical plant margins and utilisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said technical EBITDA is about 5% at 65-70% utilisation, improving about 75 bps a year, reaching up to 10% in four to five years. Analyst notes differ on the 8-10% optimum level, which management says takes two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: How does the herbicide shift affect margins and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the herbicide move is a relocation to a separate site with capacity improvement, and the Rs 50 crore capex covers units 2 and 3 this year; margin improvement is expected to reach double digits in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of El Nino and monsoon on H1 FY27 demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no impact so far in Q1 and that even distribution of rain is key; a 2-4% rainfall shortfall would not hurt the season, but an extended dry spell could.

qa_highlights.question: Export growth drivers and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports have GP of 15-20% and EBITDA of 10-12%, with new country registrations continuing and a new team created; Gulf shipments are affected but not stopped.

qa_highlights.question: Why did branded formulation grow only 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to continuous rain in Gujarat, Rajasthan and MP in August-September, where the company is strongest; other states grew.

risks_watch: Monsoon timing and distribution for Kharif 2026; June sales depend on early onset.
Raw material and input cost volatility from the West Asia crisis; inventory build raised working capital and cash conversion cycle to 87 days.
Margin dilution as lower-margin B2B and technical volumes grow faster than branded formulation.
Branded formulation recovery to 20-25% growth needs to show up in Q1 and Q2 FY27 numbers.
Herbicide facility commissioning in Q3 FY27 and ramp-up before the next Kharif season.
Export disruption in Gulf, Iran and Iraq; regulatory actions such as state-level pesticide bans.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and FY27 growth, but cautious on the near term, citing input-cost pressure and monsoon dependence. Answers to margin and split questions were often vague or inconsistent (GP vs EBITDA margins were restated during Q&A), and several questions needed repeating due to audio issues.

We believe the underlying demand environment for our brand portfolio remains intact and we expect the situation to normalize in FY'27.
The state government of Andhra Pradesh has banned paraquat. We will not have a volumetric effect.
Our EBITDA margin is around 5% for technicals.
